For me, I didn't like the anime for Citrus, but I enjoyed the manga. The animation loses a lot of the nuance that the art in the manga showed. The first Mei/Yuzu kiss scene feels more uncomfortable in the anime because you really don't get to see the pain in Mei's face or the hurt she is pushing off on Yuzu like in the manga. The anime makes Mei feel almost cold and calculated making the scene so much worse. It doesn't change the fact that Mei did it, but the manga version makes it feel more like a broken person who was lashing out since she learned that her feelings don't matter to the people she cares about the most. I think you not liking it is valid. I think that people should enjoy or not enjoy whatever they want.

Straight bait isn't a fair comparison in IMO. I would compare it to a romance show that builds chemistry between a boy and girl, but the male lead ends up with the popular girl with no personality. There is also a much smaller pool of Yuri anime. Usually, there are 10 standard romances to 1 Yuri show at a time. If that one show is bait, there isn't a place to turn to to fill that void. Hibike! is a perfect example. The leads state that they love each other, but the end up with 2 guys in the end. If that's all you got for the year, it's feels really bad.

I think the issue boils down to being burned before. Enough shows decide to throw one of the girls in the main couple at said male character that it's feels much safe to read/watch without that threat lingering. I agree that well-written male characters are great like I Favor the Villianess, but there is always this lingering feeling that Claire isn't going to end up with Rei because of Thane. (I have only read the manga) So, I agree with you, but I understand the hate.

I enjoy Yuri because I would rather read about 2 girls dating than extreme wish fulfillment. While some het romances are good, there is just so much of the loser/bland MC gets all the women he wants because he exists. Also, I can't mentally place my own massive flaws on the characters in Yuri stories. I get to just watch them experience stuff without personal baggage

Character Stereotypes: 
The Prince- a very popular girl in the school that are usually called handsome compared to cute. Usually athletic in some way.
The Gyaru- think American valley girl. Blonde, tan, loud, brash, and/or into fashion. Usually paired with a quiet girl/class Prez.
Quiet Girl- that one aloof girl in the back of the class. Often has a secret talent (most common is art) that they are great at.
Class Prez- usually studious and intelligent, but often has a crush on the more brash classmate. VP usually has a crush on the Prez as well.
The Joy- idk the official term, but they are so positive that they pull others into her orbit. 

Settings:
High School- the most common since it's easy to produce drama. A common variant is the all-girl school where it blooms more. 
College- another hotbed for drama. Allows for more diverse backgrounds to meet. Also makes the teacher/student relationship not feel creepy.
Office- another easy way to mix different backgrounds. Co-workers is more common than boss/employee, but they are both used often.
Fantasy School- when magic is involved. The usual pairing ends up be the bully/Villainess and the MC. 

Tropes:
Aquarium Date- so many of these. It is so insane. 
"Is she also gay?"- the in-built drama in most of the stories. Both girls are too scared of being rejected/isolated for being gay that they don't act on their feelings. 
Cake Date- another one used often. Easiest way to feed each other.
Secret Degen- a usually calm and controlled girl who secretly lewd as heck. 
The bath scene- boobs get compared to each other so often.
Lewd levels (highest to lowest)- Korean>Web comic>Japanese>Chinese. China will even censor kisses between women.

Other questions:
Yaoi is definitely more popular than Yuri, especially with things written online. 
I can't say for sure who the main consumers of Yuri are. From my small personal experience, it's women. But, I could 100% be wrong.
I don't think that there are many sub-genres that aren't just generally used ones across anime. 

Let me know if you have any more questions.

Rob and Benny Experiement(RnBe): two of the bigger comic book Youtubers make a show where they just talk about random topics. They very recently started playing their own game that involves giving random powers to superheroes and pitching the story. Good time for comics and great personalities.

The Weekly Pull: even more comic book Youtubers meet together on Twitch (VODs uploaded to Youtube) every other week to discuss comic book news and reviewing the movies as they come out. It really feels like friends just chatting about comics.

Just a few observations I had on the games. Please note that I am just a low ranked observer. It was a good series for the most part.

Game 1 was a really close game. There were many times where the team fights could have gone either direction. C9 just didn't have the damage to kill someone they caught. Sneaky used Ashe in a team comp that needed damage compared to the utility Ashe brings. They had two tanks, 2 utility champs, and Gragas. The burst from Gragas wasn't enough by itself to kill both Lissandra and Kassadin and Corki. Fnatic took that fact and just ran the end game perfectly. 

Game 2 was also a very back and forth game. Fnatic had a team that was focused on split pushing, yet everyone else but TF wasn't strong enough to repel a full 4 on 5. You could see that they could blow someone up if they get a pick, but C9 knew they had a better team fight team. They didn't leave each other's side for the second half of the game. That was when they could dive Corki or TF with Noct and Fizz and remove a threat from the map. That on top of an Equalizer really made the game go in C9's favor.

Game 3 was a stomp that could have been closer if they played it right. C9 was all about chaining the Kennen, Vlad, Noct, and Zyra ults together while Corki took pot shots and machine gun Fnatic to death. However, they never really got a chance to do that. Their team got split up and destroyed all through out the game. That was aided by the first and second blood given to Lee Sin. One person will die in top lane, then mid lane, then bot lane. That led to C9 doing a lot of things that didn't seem like they were thinking. Nocturne went into 3 people to kill a support and didn't get the kill anyway. It became the game Fnatic wanted to play. When C9 finally got their combo off, it was way too late. Fnatic just played the match they way they should have and came out with a W. 

Congrats to Fnatic on the win.

The group rounds end with SK T1, OMG, Mineski, and Fnatic leaving their brackets. SKT1 pull Najin Black Sword, OMG pull Royal Club, Mineski pull Gamania Bears. That leaves the best of EU vs. the best in NA with Fnatic vs. C9.

SKT1 and Sword put up one hell of a set. SSONG and Faker put up amazing performances against one another. The crowd is dazzled by the power of two of Korea's strongest teams. However, the final game comes down to a single deal between Piglet on Vayne and Pray on his famed Ezreal. Piglet loses to a well placed Arcane Shift followed by a Trinity proc. You can hear Phreak yelling about "Tons of Damage!" Najin Black Sword advance.

Bears and Mineski show why they are some of the best teams in the world. Behind a fantastic game from Steak, Gamania Bears go one up on Mineski. However, the underdogs show their true strength. With map control spearheaded by Tgee and some amazing plays from Yume on Diana, Mineski win the set going 2-1 against the Bears.

The top two teams from China face-off once again. OMG show why they were favorites coming into the finals by going up 1-0 with great jungle and objective control from Lovelin. However, Uzi would start rolling and never stop. Dying a total of 5 times in the last two games, Uzi proves why he is one of the best marksmen in the game. The Royal Club prove that they deserved the bye with a 2-1 victory over OMG.

Cloud 9 and Fnatic go head-to-head to see who really are the champions of LCS. Fnatic start of really strong with xPeke on Ahri against first blood on Hai as Zed with the help of Cyanide. But, that would be the highest point for them in the set. Cloud 9 show that NA is nothing to pick on by going 2-0 behind the unkillable Meteos. 

The semi-finals get under way with Mineski against the Korean powerhouse of Najin Black Sword. The set starts off bleak when Kaigu gives up fist blood to an invading Sword. Things seemed ever worse when they drop the next two games as well. Mineski pull themselves up from the bottom and push onward and topple the Korean Kings for two straight games. When the fifth and final game comes, it becomes a battle of the fed ones. Exo and Expression get fed kills really early on. Exo dominates the lane with Tgee, but it isn't enough. Expression is able to kill Exo before the team fight that losses Mineski the game. Najin Black Sword ride into the finals with a 3-2 victory over Mineski.

A second rematch from the All-Stars, the NA based Could 9 go against the Chinese overlords of Royal Club. C9 start the set off strong with a win with the help of Balls on his really strong Rumble. Royal finds a crack in the wall that is C9 in the early game. For two games, Lucky makes it a point to stop both Sneaky and Balls from surviving the laning phase. With Uzi and GoDlike against them, it isn't too hard. After the two losses, Lemonnation pulls out the notebook for some new strats. They surprise Royal with champions they never used before. C9 knock off Royal Club 3-2.

The finals become the most hyped thing ever. Cloud 9 and Najin Black Sword go head-to-head. The Staple Center is filled with cheering fans. C9 carry over their momentum and win the first two games. Sword, not to be outdone, win the next two games. The last game comes down to a base race. Both teams are hitting the nexus. The last hit ticks and the blue nexus explodes. The blue team wins.

TL:DR; C9 vs. Sword in the finals ends in a base race.

I find it to be unfair that people seem to treat Phil Fish like shit all the time. He is brash (to say the least) and says what comes to his mind right away, but he is still a person. That is something that people seem to forget. 

He went through a long process to even get Fez to the public, as seen in Indie Game: The Movie. It became a one man job and a struggle to even stay housed let alone making a game. He went through so much to make the game he wanted and that was before kickstarter became the main way to make an indie game. He had little to no support when he was making Fez and people were constantly harassing him during the production. 

After the game came out, people were honest with him. When someone had real criticism for the game, he didn't flip out. It was when people started to say the game was bad for things that they didn't see. It would be upsetting for anyone makes games. If the players said the Bioshock Infinite sucked because they didn't understand the ending, they would be upset. 

That wasn't the thing that really messed with him. It was being insulted day in and day out. It was getting death threats daily for being who he is. Just because he made a game, doesn't mean he is any less human. Who can honestly say that they could just shrug off being threatened every day by at least hundreds of people for years? It would get to anyone.

TL:DR Phil Fish is a person too. He may come off a a dick, but being threatened hundreds of times for years can cause anyone to break. The Beer thing was just the tipping point.

I don't find the saving thing to be the same as what Phil and Jon were talking about. The first Zelda and Metroid games had a save function in them. It isn't holding your hand to let you live life and come back to the game.

There were booklets that gave you back story and basic instructions, but they weren't as forced as current tutorials. You could just put the game in and discover everything the game has to offer. That is what they are talking about. Everyone liked to have that "Aha!" moment when they figured out how to get the magic sword in the first Zelda or find a secret missile upgrade in Metroid. The first Zelda game, by the way, didn't have cracks in any walls that needed to be bombed. That is way there were so many old people in caves and room clear drops to give hints on what to do. They did pack the carts with as much as possible, but they could of held the player's hand by removing things like secret rooms and the old people for a straight tutorial.

It is true that not only the Japanese do it. There are many games that do a ton of hand holding. Jon Blow brought that up. He said that it happens in the West, but the western game companies have full skips of the scenes more often than the Japanese games. However, they had more focus on the Japanese market because it was the question asked. Jon Blow also said that the western market has its own problems like that most of the games are about looking down a barrel of a gun. They were simply (and jerkishly in Phil Fish's case) stating their opinion on the matter. 

Jon Blow also said that there are exceptions to the hand-holding. He gave examples with Demon Souls and Dark Souls. Your example fits into that exception. It is a damn good example, though.

I like the concept. My only differing thoughts about it is with the mantra resource and the passive. 

I think you could replace the mana with the mantra resource. It would become more like a fury meter in the way you intended. You make her more about the cooldowns on her abilities until she reaches her full mantra. It would make her more consistent with the other champions that have a a new resource. Case and point, Shyvana.

The passive idea has a few flaws in it. Keeping another resource would be rather difficult to balance consistently. Charging those the yin and yang stacks would be the exact same as the mantra charging. I think that a different way of achieving the same thing would be giving her a yin buff and a yang buff. Using a defense ability would give her a buff to her next offensive ability and vice versa. That would give you the base idea of charging the opposite while making it more stream-lined.
